claims.text: A computational model integrating atomic-scale descriptors of configurational disorder, local lattice distortion, and chemical heterogeneity can identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than averaged-property models.
The target high-entropy alloys have a single-phase, highly disordered crystalline structure.
The target high-entropy alloys have a random elemental distribution.
The proposed machine-learning model incorporates detailed atomic-scale descriptors of disorder to predict phonon thermal conductivity.
Local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity enhances phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic disorder affects phonon scattering through mass fluctuations.
Atomic disorder affects phonon scattering through local strain variations.
Explicitly representing disorder-related phonon scattering makes the model more accurate than conventional averaging approaches.
The proposed model will reduce prediction error by roughly 10–20% relative to traditional methods.
Current comparison models primarily use averaged material properties and do not explicitly account for local disorder.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys maintaining a homogeneous, random elemental distribution.
The approach may not be effective in alloys with significant phase separation or ordering.
The approach may not be effective where heat-transport mechanisms other than disorder-mediated phonon transport dominate.
The estimated improvement may vary with alloy system and measurement uncertainty.
